newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares extend rebound at close on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: KL shares extend rebound at close on fund buying.

text.p: Malaysian shares bounced back on Thursday, after a week of sharp falls triggered by the central bank's curbs on property and share financing late last month, dealers and analysts said.

The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 16.80 points, or 1.54 percent, higher to 1,104.58 on selective blue-chip buying, dealers said. The index had peaked at 1,108.62 at around 0350 GMT.
"There has been buying all day," said an institutional dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage house.
"But they (institutional funds) are waiting to see how high they can go before selling," said the dealer.
Share prices had been hit by cash calls on leveraged retail clients who were forced to sell off their holdings earlier in the week.
But several clients who had suffered large losses were waiting to sell on any strong rebound, dealers said.
The Dow's firmer close on Wednesday helped boost sentiment locally, analysts said.
"Three straight days of gains have helped calm investors," said Tan Geok Hock, an analyst at Schroders in Kuala Lumpur.
